items.title: RoPE corruption due to TF32 on B200 (possibly others) when using `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("high")`
items.body:
### System Info

- `transformers` version: 4.51.3
- Platform: Linux
- Python version: 3.10.19
- PyTorch version (GPU?): torch 2.7.0a0+79aa174 (torch.version.cuda 12.9)
- GPU: reproduced on NVIDIA B200 (Blackwell, sm_100, capability 10.0); not reproduced on A100-SXM4-80GB (capability 8.0)
- Using GPU in script?: yes

### Description

The rotary-embedding angle computation

```python
freqs = (inv_freq_expanded.float() @ position_ids_expanded.float()).transpose(1, 2)
```

in `Qwen3RotaryEmbedding.forward` (and derived functions, Llama, Qwen2/3, Mistral, etc.) is a float32 matrix multiply. The surrounding `torch.autocast(..., enabled=False)` block correctly forces fp32 dtype, but does not control the multiplication backend. When `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("high")` is set, the runtime may dispatch this matmul to a GEMM tensor-core kernel which may be run in TF32 (depending on architecture). This is for example the case when ran on B200 with batch size > 1.

TF32 truncates the fp32 mantissa from 23 to 10 bits. This is problematic for the position ids: TF32 can only represent every integer exactly up to `2^11 = 2048`. Beyond that the grid spacing exceeds 1, so `position_ids` such as `2049` get truncated (to `2048`). This causes large errors in RoPE computations, see reproduction below.

#### Possible fixes

1. Locally force the fp32 backend around the angle computation:
```python
   with torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32_ctx(False):   # or set allow_tf32=False around this block
       freqs = (inv_freq_expanded.float() @ position_ids_expanded.float()).transpose(1, 2)
```

2. Avoid the matmul: 
```python
   freqs = (position_ids_expanded.float().transpose(1, 2) * inv_freq_expanded.float().transpose(1, 2))
```

I tested out both on B200/A100 and confirmed that this fixes the issue. 

#### Possibly related reports

- [thinking-machines-lab/batch_invariant_ops#23](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/batch_invariant_ops/issues/23), reproduces the identical RoPE corruption and error magnitude
- [ByteDance-Seed/VeOmni#959](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/VeOmni/pull/959)


### Who can help?

@ArthurZucker 

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

Run the following on B200:

```python
import torch
from transformers import Qwen3Config
from transformers.models.qwen3.modeling_qwen3 import Qwen3RotaryEmbedding

cfg = Qwen3Config(hidden_size=1024, num_attention_heads=8, num_key_value_heads=8,
                  head_dim=128, rope_theta=1e7, max_position_embeddings=8192)
re = Qwen3RotaryEmbedding(cfg).cuda()
pos = torch.arange(0, 4096, device="cuda")
x = torch.zeros(1, 4096, 1, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")

def cos_for(prec, bs):
    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision(prec)
    pid = pos[None, :].expand(bs, -1)          # matmul batch = bs
    with torch.no_grad():
        c, _ = re(x, pid)
    return c.float()

for bs in (1, 2, 4):
    d = (cos_for("high", bs) - cos_for("highest", bs)).abs()[:, 2048:].max().item()
    print(f"Qwen3RotaryEmbedding  bs={bs}  | high-vs-highest @2048-4096 = {d:.5f}")
```

Outputs (depending on GPU used):

```
# A100-SXM4-80GB
Qwen3RotaryEmbedding  bs=1  | high-vs-highest @2048-4096 = 0.00000
Qwen3RotaryEmbedding  bs=2  | high-vs-highest @2048-4096 = 0.00000
Qwen3RotaryEmbedding  bs=4  | high-vs-highest @2048-4096 = 0.00000

# NVIDIA B200
Qwen3RotaryEmbedding  bs=1  | high-vs-highest @2048-4096 = 0.00000
Qwen3RotaryEmbedding  bs=2  | high-vs-highest @2048-4096 = 1.28516
Qwen3RotaryEmbedding  bs=4  | high-vs-highest @2048-4096 = 1.28516

```

### Expected behavior

The RoPE angle matmul must be computed in true IEEE fp32 regardless of the global `float32_matmul_precision` setting, matching the intent of the existing `autocast(enabled=False)` guard. RoPE output numbers between GPU architectures should match (up to corresponding floating point precision).

items.title: fix: apply _rope_type_labels override to validate_rope for Gemma3 and Olmo3
items.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48427&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48427) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48427&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48427)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?


'validate_rope' was incorrectly wrapping nested RoPE config dictionary in modeling_rope_utils.py. This occurs because the 2 conditions within the if line at 828 contradict themselves during edge cases, the fault lies in the line set(rope_parameters_dict.keys()).issubset(self.layer_types).
The first function would call the dictionary key {"sliding_attention", "full_attention"} and the second function would check the keys if they're in the actual layers [sliding_attention", "full_attention"].
The answer here would be False because "full_attention" is missing from the actual layers. This occurs in smaller experimental models where there's not enough layers for a full_attention to occur.
For instance, in configuration_olmo3.py, around line 94-97, we get the code: "sliding_attention" if (i + 1) % 4 != 0 else "full_attention" for i in range(self.num_hidden_layers)
That basically means every 4th layer it will be a full_attention, but in the event of smaller model like hidden layers being just 2, there would not be a full_attention layer, thus triggering a "unrecognized key" error.
In the same util file, we could look up and see the configuration being used by Deepseek V4 being applicable here, using _rope_type_labels. The mechanic is pretty simple: First it copies the line "getattr(self, "_rope_type_labels", ...) logic down into the function validate_rope so both share the same function math. Then it adds _rope_type_labels = ["sliding_attention", "full_attention"] to Gemma3 config file so it can use the same override switch like DeepSeek did. 
Originally, I saw the logic error in the line set(rope_parameters_dict.keys()).issubset(self.layer_types) and intended to simply invert the conditions with set(self.layer_types).issubset(rope_parameters_dict.keys()), but I figured it would be better to follow the configuration pattern in the file.

items.title: Fix per-layer rope_parameters misparsing when layer_types omits keys
items.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48411&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48411) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48411&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48411)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #48392.

### Problem
Models that use heterogeneous attention layers (e.g. `Gemma3`, `Olmo3` mixing sliding and full attention) populate `rope_parameters` with entries for every possible layer type (`sliding_attention` and `full_attention`). However, when a model configuration is instantiated with fewer layers than the sliding window period (such as `Gemma3TextConfig(num_hidden_layers=2)` or `Olmo3Config(num_hidden_layers=2)`), `config.layer_types` contains only `["sliding_attention", "sliding_attention"]`.

Previously, `standardize_rope_params` and `validate_rope` checked `set(rope_parameters.keys()).issubset(layer_types)`. When not all layer types were instantiated, this check returned `False`, causing the nested dictionary to be misclassified as a single flat config dict:
1. Emitting a spurious warning: `Unrecognized keys in rope_parameters for 'rope_type'='default': {'full_attention', 'sliding_attention'}`.
2. Polluting `config.rope_parameters` with top-level `"rope_type": "default"` and `"rope_theta": None` which was then persisted to disk on `save_pretrained`.
3. Bypassing validation of actual per-layer RoPE parameters (e.g., `yarn`, `linear`) for non-instantiated layer types.

### Solution
- In `src/transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py`, validate that `rope_parameters` keys are a subset of `allowed_layer_types` (checking `_rope_type_labels` if present, or `ALLOWED_LAYER_TYPES` from `configuration_utils.py`) rather than only currently instantiated `self.layer_types`.
- In `standardize_rope_params`, iterate over `set(rope_parameters.keys())` so all configured layer types are standardized.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `tests/utils/test_modeling_rope_utils.py` verifying clean standardization, warning suppression, validation, and `save_pretrained`/`from_pretrained` round-tripping for partial layer configurations.

### What does this PR do?

→ `nomic_bert` and `jina_embeddings_v3` are the only two RoPE encoders that carry BERT's [buffered token_type_ids gather](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/42ca97014c85d71a88ad60d55f08cb9fb4d26e2c/src/transformers/models/bert/modeling_bert.py#L89-L96). The buffer is all zeros, so the gather is a no-op, but indexing it with `position_ids` still constrains those IDs to `max_position_embeddings`, which RoPE has no reason to obey. Both original implementations build the zeros directly ([nomic](https://huggingface.co/nomic-ai/nomic-bert-2048/blob/7710840340a098cfb869c4f65e87cf2b1b70caca/modeling_hf_nomic_bert.py#L1015-L1019), [jina](https://huggingface.co/jinaai/xlm-roberta-flash-implementation/blob/bd55a5ec8e6c0fb1d6c26efb4b6a4a74ce8a88d3/embedding.py#L91-L94)) and nomic sets [max_position_embeddings = 0](https://huggingface.co/nomic-ai/nomic-bert-2048/blob/7710840340a098cfb869c4f65e87cf2b1b70caca/modeling_hf_nomic_bert.py#L993) whenever rotary is on, so the cap tmk isn't upstream behaviour either.
→ In practice this caps `nomic-embed-text-v1.5` at 2048 tokens on `main` (`RuntimeError: index 2048 is out of bounds for dimension 1 with size 2048`) despite `n_positions: 8192`; it reaches 8192 here. Un-skips `test_model_rope_scaling_from_config` for nomic, which passes now :)

cc: @vasqu
